groups.title: Tablet (A21200ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the supply of vitamin C in physical tiredness, during pregnancy and breast-feeding and when strength is reduced during or after illness, for the relief of pigmentation (melasma, freckles) caused by sunlight or skin disease, and for the prevention of bleeding gums and nosebleed.
groups.usage: Children aged 8 years and older and adults: take 1 tablet, 1 time in 1 day.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if the user is a baby under 3 months of age; if you have had hypersensitivity or an allergic reaction to soybean oil; or if you have hypersensitivity to soybean or peanut.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; if the user is a premature baby or a young child; if you have hyperoxaluria; if you have gout or kidney stones; or if you have a disorder of fat metabolism such as hyperlipoproteinaemia, diabetic hyperlipidaemia or pancreatitis, or lipid emulsions must be given to you with caution.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. When it is given to a child, use it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian. It may interfere with the detection of sugar in various urine tests.

If nausea, vomiting or diarrhoea occurs, or if symptoms do not improve after about 1 month of use, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

summaryTable.What it is for: Supply of vitamin C, relief of pigmentation such as melasma and freckles, and prevention of bleeding gums and nosebleed

summaryTable.Ask the pharmacist: Ask the pharmacist in the store first if any of the cautions above apply to you.

groups.title: Soft Capsule (E58700ACS)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for pain relief in headache, toothache, pain after tooth extraction, sore throat, earache, joint pain, neuralgia, back pain, muscle pain, stiff shoulders, bruise pain, fracture pain, sprain pain, menstrual pain (period pain) and pain from injury, and for reducing fever with chills.
groups.usage: Adults and those aged 15 years and older: take 1 to 2 capsules per dose. Ages 8 years to under 15 years: take 1 capsule per dose. Take it 1 to 3 times in 1 day, avoiding an empty stomach. Leave an interval of at least 4 hours between doses.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day, consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause gastrointestinal bleeding.

People with uncontrolled high blood pressure, congestive heart failure, established ischaemic heart disease, peripheral arterial disease or cerebrovascular disease must avoid high-dose ibuprofen (2,400 mg a day); people with cardiovascular risk factors (high blood pressure, high blood lipids, diabetes, smoking and the like) who need high-dose ibuprofen (2,400 mg a day) must consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine.

Do not take this medicine if you have or have had hypersensitivity to it; if you have had asthma after taking this medicine, one of its ingredients, another antipyretic analgesic or a cold medicine; if the user is a baby under 3 months of age; if you have had hypersensitivity or an allergic reaction to soybean oil; if you have hypersensitivity to soybean or peanut; or if you are 30 weeks or more pregnant.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if the user is a baby or a child under 15 years of age who has had, or is suspected of having, chickenpox or influenza; if you have an allergic constitution or have had an allergic reaction (fever, rash, joint pain, asthma, itching and the like); if you have liver disease, kidney disease, thyroid disease, diabetes or high blood pressure; if you are physically weak or have a high fever; if you are an older person; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; if you have stomach problems such as heartburn, stomach discomfort or stomach pain, or an ulcer or bleeding problem; if you have lost a lot of fluid through vomiting and diarrhoea, are not taking in fluid or are taking a diuretic; if you have a disorder of fat metabolism such as hyperlipoproteinaemia, diabetic hyperlipidaemia or pancreatitis, or lipid emulsions must be given to you with caution, or you have fat overload; if the user is a child under 2 years of age; or if you are 20 to 30 weeks pregnant.

If symptoms do not improve after 5 to 6 doses, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist. Keep to the stated dosage and schedule.

Do not take it together with another antipyretic analgesic, a cold medicine or a sedative. Consult a pharmacist if you take it together with low-dose aspirin, an intravenous lipid preparation or a product containing ibuprofen.

If rash, reddening of the skin, itching, nausea, vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, stomach pain, gastrointestinal bleeding, stomach discomfort, dizziness, oedema, or, rarely, signs of shock (urticaria, swelling and chest tightness soon after taking it, together with pallor, cold hands and feet, cold sweat and difficulty breathing), Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (with high fever, rash and reddening of the skin and severe burn-like blisters on the skin of the whole body or on the mouth or eye membranes), asthma, very rarely erythema multiforme or exfoliative dermatitis, or a photosensitivity reaction, drug reaction with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS syndrome), acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis or Conn's syndrome of unknown frequency occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.title: Tablet (E76800ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for excess stomach acid, heartburn, stomach discomfort, a feeling of fullness in the stomach, indigestion with a feeling of stuffiness, nausea, vomiting, stomach pain, acid eructation (sour belching), indigestion, loss of appetite, overeating, promotion of digestion, and a feeling of fullness in the stomach caused by indigestion.
groups.usage: Adults: take 2 tablets per dose, 3 times in 1 day, between meals.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you are on dialysis; if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption; if the user is a child under 15 years of age; or if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have or have had an allergy (rash, reddening of the skin, itching and the like); if you have kidney impairment, liver impairment or low blood phosphate; if you have high blood pressure or are an older person; if you have heart or kidney impairment; or if you have oedema.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. If symptoms do not improve after about 2 weeks of use, stop using it immediately and consult a pharmacist. Do not use it continuously for a long period.

Do not take it together with a gastrointestinal analgesic or antispasmodic. Consult a pharmacist if you take it together with a potassium-containing preparation, a liquorice-containing preparation, a preparation containing glycyrrhizic acid or its salts, a loop diuretic (furosemide, etacrynic acid) or a thiazide diuretic (trichlormethiazide).

If reduced urine volume, swelling of the face, hands or feet, heavy eyelids, stiff hands, raised blood pressure, headache, pseudoaldosteronism (low blood potassium, raised blood pressure, retention of sodium and body fluid, oedema, weight gain), myopathy (weakness, cramps of the limbs, paralysis), allergic symptoms (rash, itching and the like), or, rarely, palpitations, drowsiness, dizziness, lassitude, headache, constipation, dry mouth, a racing heartbeat or raised GOT and GPT occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

summaryTable.What it is for: Excess stomach acid, heartburn, stomach discomfort and fullness, indigestion, nausea, vomiting, stomach pain, sour belching, loss of appetite and overeating

groups.title: Soft Capsule (A02400ACS)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the supply of vitamin E in old age, for the relief of peripheral circulatory disturbance and of stiffness of the shoulders and neck and numbness and coldness of the hands and feet around the menopause, and for muscle cramps caused by magnesium deficiency.
groups.usage: Adults aged 18 years and older: take 1 capsule per dose, 2 times in 1 day.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it or to soybean oil, soybean or peanut; if the user is a baby under 12 months of age; or if you have severe renal failure.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; if the user is a premature baby or a young child; if you have impaired heart or circulatory function, kidney impairment or hypoproteinaemia; if you have a disorder of fat metabolism such as hyperlipoproteinaemia, diabetic hyperlipidaemia or pancreatitis, or lipid emulsions must be given to you with caution; if you are at particular risk from fat overload; or if you have a tendency to thrombosis (blocked blood vessels).

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule.

Do not take it together with a phosphate, a calcium salt, an oral tetracycline preparation or an antacid. Consult a pharmacist if you use it together with an oral contraceptive containing oestrogen, an antialdosterone medicine, triamterene or an intravenous lipid preparation. Avoid tannin-containing drinks such as green tea and black tea while taking it and just before and after taking it.

If stomach discomfort, diarrhoea, constipation, rash (reddening of the skin), red spots, cardiac arrest or reduced central nervous system function occurs, or if menstruation comes earlier than expected, becomes heavier or bleeding lasts longer, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.title: Soft Capsule (185401ACS)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for allergic rhinitis (sneezing, blocked nose, itching, burning of the eyes) and for chronic idiopathic urticaria.
groups.usage: Adults and children aged 12 years and older: take 1 tablet (10 mg) per dose, 1 time in 1 day. Ages 6 to under 12 years whose body weight is 30 kg or more: take 1 tablet (10 mg) per dose, 1 time in 1 day.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if the user is a child under 6 years of age; or if you are pregnant or breast-feeding.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have liver impairment or renal failure.

Do not take it together with cimetidine, erythromycin, ketoconazole, quinidine, fluconazole or fluoxetine.

If sedation, anticholinergic effects, headache, fainting, drowsiness, thirst, gastrointestinal disturbance (nausea, gastritis), increased appetite, rapid heartbeat, fatigue, rash, hair loss, anaphylaxis including angioedema, liver function disorder, supraventricular tachyarrhythmia, palpitations, dizziness or convulsions occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

summaryTable.What it is for: Allergic rhinitis and chronic idiopathic urticaria

groups.title: Tablet (101404ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for fever and pain caused by a cold, headache, neuralgia, muscle pain, menstrual pain, pain from a sprain, toothache, joint pain and rheumatic pain.
groups.usage: Adults: take 300 to 1000 mg per dose, 3 to 4 times in 1 day. Up to 4000 mg may be given in 1 day. The dose may be increased or decreased appropriately according to age and symptoms.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day, consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause liver damage.

This medicine contains aspartame, which is metabolised in the body to phenylalanine, so it must not be taken by people with phenylketonuria who need to restrict their intake of phenylalanine.

Very rarely, serious skin reactions that may be fatal, such as acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis, have been reported. If a skin rash or any other sign of hypersensitivity appears after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.

Do not exceed the maximum daily dose of acetaminophen (4,000 mg). It may cause liver damage. Do not take it together with other products that contain acetaminophen.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it, peptic ulcer, a severe blood disorder, severe liver impairment, severe kidney impairment or severely reduced heart function; if you have or have had aspirin asthma (an asthma attack triggered by a non-steroidal anti-inflammatory medicine); or if you have taken barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants or alcohol.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have or have had liver impairment or kidney impairment; if you have had peptic ulcer; if you have or have had a blood disorder; if you have a tendency to bleed; if you have impaired heart function; if you have bronchial asthma; if you are an older person; or if you are pregnant or breast-feeding.

Do not take it together with other products containing acetaminophen, another anti-inflammatory analgesic, barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants or alcohol. Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you take it together with warfarin, lithium or a thiazide diuretic.

If signs of shock (difficulty breathing, flushing of the whole body, angioedema, urticaria, an asthma attack and the like), thrombocytopenia, granulocytopenia, haemolytic anaemia, methaemoglobinaemia, reduced platelet function (prolonged bleeding time), cyanosis, nausea, vomiting, loss of appetite, gastrointestinal bleeding, peptic ulcer, perforation, hypersensitivity symptoms (facial swelling, sweating, low blood pressure), rash, Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), abnormal liver function such as raised AST or raised ALT, or fixed drug eruption occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.title: Tablet (162601ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the prevention and treatment of folic acid deficiency, for wasting disease, for supply when the need for folic acid is increased in pregnancy and breast-feeding and intake from food is insufficient, as an aid in the treatment of pernicious anaemia (excluding anaemia caused by vitamin B12 deficiency), for nutritional deficiency anaemia, anaemia of pregnancy, anaemia in children and anaemia caused by antiepileptic treatment in which folic acid deficiency or a metabolic disturbance is thought to be involved, and for megaloblastic anaemia related to alcoholism and liver disease.
groups.usage: For the treatment of folic acid deficiency and of deficiency caused by other medicines, adults and children aged 24 months and older: take 0.25 to 1 mg in 1 day. For the prevention of folic acid deficiency and for conditions in which the requirement for folic acid is increased, adults and children aged 24 months and older: take 0.1 to 0.25 mg in 1 day.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if you have pernicious anaemia or megaloblastic anaemia caused by vitamin B12 deficiency; or if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have pernicious anaemia.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. When it is given to a child, use it under the supervision of a guardian. If symptoms do not improve after about 1 month of use, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

Consult a pharmacist if you are taking aminosalicylic acid, an oral contraceptive, a dihydrofolate reductase inhibitor (methotrexate, trimethoprim and the like), a hydantoin antiepileptic such as phenytoin, sulfasalazine or cholestyramine.

If allergic symptoms such as erythema, skin rash, itching, general lassitude or difficulty breathing, an anaphylactic reaction, loss of appetite, nausea and vomiting, oedema, weight loss, gastrointestinal disturbance, or central nervous system disturbance such as changes in sleep, poor concentration, hyperactivity, irritability, excitement, depression, confusion or impaired judgement occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

Do not take it together with another antipyretic analgesic, a cold medicine or a sedative.

If rash and reddening of the skin, nausea, vomiting, constipation, loss of appetite or vertigo occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.title: Soft Capsule (E72100ACS)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the relief of the various symptoms of a cold (runny nose, blocked nose, sneezing, sore throat, cough, phlegm, chills with shivering, fever, headache, joint pain, muscle pain).
groups.usage: Adults and those aged 15 years and older: take it 3 times in 1 day, 2 capsules per dose, 30 minutes after meals.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day, consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause liver damage.

Very rarely, serious skin reactions that may be fatal, such as acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis, have been reported. If a skin rash or any other sign of hypersensitivity appears after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.

Do not exceed the maximum daily dose of acetaminophen (4,000 mg). It may cause liver damage. Do not take it together with other products that contain acetaminophen.

If a severe skin adverse reaction such as acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis occurs, stop taking it and consult a pharmacist.

Do not take this medicine if you have or have had hypersensitivity to it; if you have had asthma after taking this medicine, one of its ingredients, another antipyretic analgesic or a cold medicine; if the user is a baby (newborn) under 3 months of age; or if you have severe or uncontrolled high blood pressure.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if the user is a child under 2 years of age; if the user is a baby (newborn) or a child under 15 years of age with, or suspected of having, chickenpox or influenza; if ischaemic colitis (sudden abdominal pain, rectal bleeding and the like) occurs in connection with pseudoephedrine; if you have a constitution prone to urticaria, contact dermatitis, bronchial asthma, allergic rhinitis, migraine or food allergy, or have had an allergic reaction (for example fever, rash, joint pain, asthma or itching); if you have liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, gastric or duodenal ulcer, glaucoma (for example eye pain or blurred vision) or difficulty passing urine; if you are an older person, physically weak or have a high fever; if you have persistent or recurring stomach problems such as heartburn, stomach discomfort or stomach pain, or an ulcer or bleeding problem; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; or if you have a cough (smoking, asthma, chronic bronchitis, emphysema, a cough with excessive sputum, a cough lasting or recurring for 1 week or more, a chronic cough, or a cough with fever, rash or persistent headache).

If symptoms do not improve after 5 to 6 doses, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist. Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. Drowsiness may occur after taking it, so take care when driving or operating machinery.

Do not take it together with an antitussive-expectorant, another cold medicine, an antipyretic analgesic, a sedative, an oral medicine containing an antihistamine (oral medicine for rhinitis, motion-sickness medicine, anti-allergy medicine) or an MAO inhibitor. Do not take this medicine if you have stopped taking an MAO inhibitor (antidepressant, antipsychotic, mood stabiliser, anti-Parkinson medicine and the like) within the past 2 weeks. Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you are being given another medicine such as a diabetes medicine, a gout medicine, an arthritis medicine, an anticoagulant or a steroid. In people given barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants or alcohol, the ability to metabolise a large amount of acetaminophen is reduced and the plasma half-life of acetaminophen may be increased, so take care. Do not drink alcohol while taking it.

If rash and reddening of the skin, itching, nausea and vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, oedema, difficulty passing urine, persistent or severe thirst, dizziness, anxiety, tremor, insomnia, or, rarely, shock (urticaria, swelling, chest tightness, pallor, cold hands and feet, cold sweat, difficulty breathing and the like), Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), asthma, general lassitude, jaundice (yellowing of the skin or the whites of the eyes) or interstitial pneumonia occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

If symptoms of posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome or reversible cerebral vasoconstriction syndrome (sudden severe headache, thunderclap headache, nausea, vomiting, confusion, seizure, visual disturbance and the like) occur, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for pain relief in headache, toothache, pain after tooth extraction, sore throat, earache, joint pain, neuralgia, back pain, muscle pain, stiff shoulders, bruise pain, fracture pain, sprain pain, period pain and pain from injury, and for reducing fever with chills.
groups.usage: Adults and those aged 15 years and older: take 1 capsule per dose, 1 to 3 times in 1 day, leaving an interval of at least 4 hours, and avoid taking it on an empty stomach.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day, consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause gastrointestinal bleeding.

People with uncontrolled high blood pressure, congestive heart failure, established ischaemic heart disease, peripheral arterial disease or cerebrovascular disease should use ibuprofen only after careful consideration and should avoid high-dose ibuprofen (2,400 mg a day). Also, if a person with cardiovascular risk factors (for example high blood pressure, high blood lipids, diabetes or smoking) needs high-dose ibuprofen (2,400 mg a day), consider this carefully before starting long-term treatment. Clinical studies have shown that use of high-dose ibuprofen (2,400 mg a day) may slightly increase the risk of arterial thrombotic events (myocardial infarction or stroke).

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if you have had asthma after taking another antipyretic analgesic or a cold medicine; or if the user is a baby under 3 months of age.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if the user is a baby or a child under 15 years of age with, or suspected of having, chickenpox or influenza; if you have an allergic constitution or have had allergic symptoms caused by a medicine (for example fever, rash, joint pain, asthma or itching); if you have liver disease, kidney disease, thyroid disease, diabetes or high blood pressure; if you are physically weak or have a high fever; if you are an older person; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; if you have stomach problems such as heartburn, stomach discomfort or stomach pain, or an ulcer or bleeding problem; if you have lost a lot of fluid through vomiting and diarrhoea or are not taking in fluid; or if the user is a child under 2 years of age.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. If symptoms do not improve after 5 to 6 doses, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

Do not take it together with another antipyretic analgesic, a cold medicine or a sedative. Consult a pharmacist if you take it together with a diabetes medicine, a gout medicine, an arthritis medicine, an anticoagulant, a steroid, low-dose aspirin or a diuretic. Do not drink alcohol while taking it.

If rash and reddening of the skin, itching, nausea and vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, stomach pain, gastrointestinal bleeding, stomach discomfort, dizziness, swelling, or, rarely, signs of shock (urticaria, swelling and chest tightness soon after taking it, together with pallor, cold hands and feet, cold sweat and difficulty breathing), Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (with high fever, rash and reddening of the skin and severe burn-like blisters on the skin of the whole body and on the mouth or eye membranes), asthma, very rarely erythema multiforme or exfoliative dermatitis, or a photosensitivity reaction, drug reaction with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS syndrome) or acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis of unknown frequency occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

summaryTable.What it is for: Pain relief in headache, toothache, sore throat, earache, joint, nerve, back, muscle and shoulder pain, bruises, fractures, sprains, period pain and injury pain, and reducing fever

groups.title: Tablet (E68900ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the supply of vitamin C in physical tiredness, during pregnancy and breast-feeding and when strength is reduced during or after illness, and for the supply of zinc and selenium.
groups.usage: Adults and those aged 12 years and older: take 1 tablet per dose, 2 times in 1 day, or 2 tablets per dose, 1 time in 1 day.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if the user is a baby under 12 months of age; or if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have hyperoxaluria; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; if the user is a premature baby or a young child; if you have a gastrointestinal disease such as peptic ulcer, chronic ulcerative colitis or regional enteritis; if you have impaired heart or circulatory function, kidney impairment or hypoproteinaemia; if you have gallbladder-related disease or liver disease; or if you have diabetes, gout or kidney stones.

If symptoms do not improve after about 1 month of use, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist. Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. It may interfere with the detection of sugar in various urine tests.

Do not take it together with a phosphate, a calcium salt, an oral tetracycline preparation or an antacid. Consult a pharmacist if you use it together with an antialdosterone medicine or triamterene. Avoid tannin-containing drinks such as green tea and black tea while taking it and just before and after taking it.

If nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, dermatitis, a bad smell in the sweat or breath, hair loss, irritability, gastrointestinal disturbance, digestive disturbance, upper abdominal pain, low blood pressure or pulmonary oedema occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.title: Soft Capsule (D08400ACS)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the relief of the various symptoms of a cold (sore throat, cough, phlegm, chills with shivering, fever, headache, joint pain, muscle pain).
groups.usage: Adults and those aged 15 years and older: take 2 capsules per dose. Ages 8 years to under 15 years: take 1 capsule per dose. Take it 3 times in 1 day, 30 minutes after meals.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day, consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause liver damage.

Very rarely, serious skin reactions that may be fatal, such as acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis, have been reported. If a skin rash or any other sign of hypersensitivity appears after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.

Do not exceed the maximum daily dose of acetaminophen (4,000 mg). It may cause liver damage. Do not take it together with other products that contain acetaminophen.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if you have had asthma after taking another antipyretic analgesic or a cold medicine; if the user is a baby under 3 months of age; or if you are taking an MAO inhibitor (antidepressant, antipsychotic, mood stabiliser, anti-Parkinson medicine and the like) or have stopped taking one within the past 2 weeks.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if the user is a baby or a child under 15 years of age with, or suspected of having, chickenpox or influenza; if the user is a baby or young child aged 3 months or older and under 2 years of age; if you have an allergic constitution; if you have liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure or gastric or duodenal ulcer; if you are an older person, physically weak or have a high fever; if you have persistent or recurring stomach problems such as heartburn, stomach discomfort or stomach pain, or an ulcer or bleeding problem; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; or if you smoke or have asthma, chronic bronchitis, emphysema, a cough with excessive sputum, a cough lasting or recurring for 1 week or more, a chronic cough, or a cough with fever, rash or persistent headache.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. When it is given to a child, use it under the supervision of a guardian. Do not take it continuously for a long period. Do not drink alcohol while taking it. If symptoms do not improve after 5 to 6 doses, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

Do not take it together with other products containing acetaminophen, an MAO inhibitor (antidepressant, antipsychotic, mood stabiliser, anti-Parkinson medicine and the like), an antitussive-expectorant, another cold medicine, an antipyretic analgesic, a sedative, or an oral medicine containing an antihistamine (oral medicine for rhinitis, motion-sickness medicine, anti-allergy medicine). Consult a pharmacist if you have been given a diabetes medicine, a gout medicine, an arthritis medicine, an anticoagulant, a steroid, barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants or alcohol. Do not drink alcohol while taking it.

If rash and reddening of the skin, itching, nausea and vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, oedema, dizziness, anxiety, tremor, insomnia, signs of shock (urticaria, swelling and chest tightness soon after taking it, together with pallor, cold hands and feet, cold sweat and difficulty breathing), Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome, with high fever, rash and reddening of the skin and severe burn-like blisters), acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis, a severe skin adverse reaction such as fever, erythema and many small pustules, asthma, general lassitude, jaundice (yellowing of the skin or the whites of the eyes) or interstitial pneumonia (cough, breathlessness, difficulty breathing, fever) occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

Through the vitamins it contains, this medicine is used for the relief of neuralgia, muscle pain, back pain, joint pain such as stiff shoulders, angular cheilitis, cheilitis, stomatitis, glossitis, eczema and dermatitis. Through the vitamins it contains, this medicine is used for poor development of the bones and teeth, for the prevention of rickets, and for beriberi and eye strain.
groups.usage: Adults aged 19 years and older: take 1 tablet per dose, 1 time in 1 day.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it or to soybean or peanut; if you have or have had hypersensitivity to soybean oil; if the user is a baby under 12 months of age; if you have high blood calcium, sarcoidosis, kidney disease, kidney stones or severe renal failure; or if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; if the user is a premature baby or a young child; if you have impaired heart or circulatory function or kidney impairment; if you have had kidney stones; if you have hypoproteinaemia; if you have a disorder of fat metabolism such as hyperlipoproteinaemia, diabetic hyperlipidaemia or pancreatitis, or lipid emulsions must be given to you with caution; or if you have fat overload.

If symptoms do not improve after about 1 month of use, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist. If you are short of folic acid, consult a pharmacist. It may turn the urine yellow and so affect clinical test values. Keep to the stated dosage and schedule.

While you are taking this medicine, do not take a phosphate, a calcium salt, an oral tetracycline preparation, an antacid, levodopa and the like. Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you are being given a cardiac glycoside. Consult a pharmacist if you take it together with an antialdosterone medicine or triamterene. Avoid tannin-containing drinks such as green tea and black tea while taking it and just before and after taking it.

If nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, loose stools, constipation, low blood pressure, facial flushing, an irregular heartbeat, skin rash, red spots, cardiac arrest, reduced central nervous system function, loss of appetite, erythema, eczema, rash, maculopapular rash, itching, oedema, or fluid retention in people with kidney failure or heart failure occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. It may interfere with the detection of sugar in various urine tests, and it may turn the urine yellow and so affect clinical test values. If symptoms do not improve after about 1 month of use, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.title: Capsule (E04100ACH)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the relief of blocked nose, runny nose, sneezing, watering eyes, throat pain and a heavy head caused by a nasal cold (acute rhinitis), allergic rhinitis or sinusitis.
groups.usage: Adults and those aged 15 years and older: take 1 capsule per dose, 3 times in 1 day, after each meal.
groups.caution:
If a severe skin adverse reaction such as acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis occurs, stop taking it and consult a pharmacist.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if the user is a child under 15 years of age; if you are pregnant or breast-feeding; if you are an older person (aged 65 years and older); if you are taking an MAO inhibitor (antidepressant, antipsychotic, mood stabiliser, anti-Parkinson medicine and the like) or have stopped taking one within the past 2 weeks; or if you have high blood pressure, heart disease, thyroid dysfunction, diabetes, glaucoma, prostatic hyperplasia, kidney disease, epilepsy or hepatitis.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have had an allergy caused by a medicine; if a cold medicine, an antitussive-expectorant or an oral medicine for rhinitis has ever caused insomnia, vertigo, weakness, tremor or palpitations; or if you smoke or have asthma, chronic bronchitis, emphysema, a cough with excessive sputum, a cough lasting or recurring for 1 week or more, a chronic cough, or a cough with fever, rash or persistent headache.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. Do not take it continuously for a long period. When it is given to someone aged 15 years and older who is still a child, use it under the supervision of a guardian. Drowsiness may occur after taking it, so take care when driving or operating machinery. If symptoms do not improve after 5 to 6 doses, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

Do not take it together with an MAO inhibitor (antidepressant, antipsychotic, mood stabiliser, anti-Parkinson medicine and the like), another oral medicine for rhinitis, or an oral medicine containing an antihistamine (cold medicine, antitussive-expectorant, motion-sickness medicine, anti-allergy medicine and the like). Do not drink alcohol while taking it.

If haemorrhagic stroke, nausea, vomiting, persistent or severe thirst, constipation, loss of appetite, rash, reddening of the skin, itching, difficulty passing urine, headache, facial flushing, abnormal sensitivity to light, signs of shock, or ischaemic colitis (sudden abdominal pain, rectal bleeding) occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have had allergic symptoms such as rash, reddening of the skin or itching; if you have kidney impairment, liver impairment or heart impairment; if you have low blood phosphate or oedema; if you have high blood pressure; if you are an older person; or if you have had kidney disease.

If symptoms do not improve after about 2 weeks of use, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist. Keep to the stated dosage and schedule.

groups.title: Tablet (106301ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for acute and chronic bronchitis and asthmatic bronchitis caused by disturbance of mucus secretion.
groups.usage: Adults: take 1 tablet (30 mg) per dose, 3 times in 1 day, with or without food. When treatment is continued, take 1 tablet (30 mg) per dose, 2 times in 1 day.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it, severe kidney impairment or severe liver impairment, or if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have kidney impairment or peptic ulcer, if you are pregnant or breast-feeding, or if you are an older person.

Consult a pharmacist if you take it together with an antibiotic such as erythromycin, cefalexin, oxytetracycline, amoxicillin, cefuroxime or doxycycline.

If any of the following occur, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist: serious skin damage such as Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome) or toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome); fever, itching, rhinitis, and non-specific influenza-like prodromal symptoms such as cough and sore throat; commonly nausea; uncommonly vomiting, diarrhoea, indigestion, abdominal pain, heartburn, dry mouth, stomach discomfort, a feeling of fullness in the stomach or abdomen, constipation, loss of appetite, urticaria, skin rash, an anaphylactic reaction (including anaphylactic shock), urticarial erythema, angioedema, itching or other hypersensitivity reactions, swelling of the face, difficulty breathing, a rise in body temperature with chills, purulent rhinitis with a raised white blood cell count, abnormal sensation of the tongue, a change in taste, numbness in the mouth or a feeling of numbness in the arm.
